title: Crowd Evacuation Through Building Exits with Time Control
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that simulates a crowd evacuation through a building with multiple exits and full time control.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 50, 60) looking down at the floor plan at angle (-0.7, 0, 0).
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light from (20, 40, 20) with intensity 0.8 and shadow mapping enabled.
- The floor is a 60x40 rectangular plane (gray, #888888) centered at origin, representing a building hall.
- Create 4 walls as thin box geometries (dark gray #444444) along the edges of the floor, each wall 2 units tall.
- Cut 3 exits (gaps) into the walls: Exit A on the left wall at z=0 (width 4), Exit B on the right wall at z=0 (width 4), Exit C on the bottom wall (positive z side) at x=0 (width 6). Each exit is a gap in the wall geometry.
- Mark each exit with a green (#00ff44) emissive strip on the floor at the gap location.

## Agents (Crowd)
- Spawn exactly 80 agents as small sphere meshes (radius 0.4) at random positions inside the building floor bounds (with 2-unit margin from walls).
- Color agents by their assigned exit: red (#ff3333) for Exit A, blue (#3366ff) for Exit B, yellow (#ffcc00) for Exit C.
- Each agent is assigned to the nearest exit at spawn time.
- Agents move toward their assigned exit at a base speed of 3.0 units/second, with a small random offset (±0.5) per agent for variation.
- Implement simple collision avoidance: agents repel each other when within 1.2 units distance using a repulsion force vector scaled by 2.0.
- Agents that reach within 1.5 units of their exit center are removed from the scene (evacuated).
- Agents must not pass through walls; clamp positions to stay within floor bounds except at exit gaps.

## Physics & Simulation
- Use a fixed timestep of 1/60 second for simulation updates.
- Multiply the effective dt by a timeScale factor (default 1.0).
- Track simulation elapsed time separately from real time.
- Enforce: no agent position may ever be NaN. If detected, reset that agent to the building center.
- Track total distance traveled by all agents combined (sum of per-frame displacements).

## Time Control
- Keyboard 'Space' toggles pause/resume of the simulation.
- Keyboard 'ArrowUp' increases timeScale by 0.5 (max 5.0).
- Keyboard 'ArrowDown' decreases timeScale by 0.5 (min 0.0).
- Keyboard 'R' resets the entire simulation: re-spawn all 80 agents at NEW random positions, reset elapsed time to 0, reset evacuated counts to 0, set timeScale to 1.0, unpause.
- Keyboard 'U' performs UNDO of the last speed change (reverts timeScale to its previous value before the last ArrowUp/ArrowDown). Maintain a history stack of timeScale values (max depth 20).
- Keyboard 'B' toggles blockade mode for Exit B: when blocked, agents assigned to Exit B are reassigned to the nearest open exit, and the green strip for Exit B turns red (#ff0000). Pressing 'B' again reopens it and reassigns agents back if they haven't evacuated.

## HUD / DOM Elements
- Create a HUD overlay div (id='hud') at top-left with the following info, updated every frame:
  - 'Agents Remaining: XX' (id='agentsRemaining')
  - 'Evacuated: XX' (id='evacuatedCount')
  - 'Sim Time: XX.Xs' (id='simTime', one decimal)
  - 'Time Scale: X.Xx' (id='timeScale', two decimals)
  - 'Paused: Yes/No' (id='pausedStatus')
  - 'Exit B Blocked: Yes/No' (id='exitBBlocked')
- Add a DOM button (id='btnReset') labeled 'Reset Simulation' that triggers the same reset as 'R' key.
- Add a DOM button (id='btnToggleExitB') labeled 'Toggle Exit B' that triggers the same action as 'B' key.

## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose and continuously update the following on window.__3D_STATE__:
- `agentCount` (number): current agents remaining in scene
- `evacuatedTotal` (number): total agents evacuated
- `evacuatedA` (number): agents evacuated through Exit A
- `evacuatedB` (number): agents evacuated through Exit B
- `evacuatedC` (number): agents evacuated through Exit C
- `simTime` (number): simulation elapsed time in seconds
- `timeScale` (number): current time scale multiplier
- `paused` (boolean): whether simulation is paused
- `exitBBlocked` (boolean): whether Exit B is currently blocked
- `totalDistanceTraveled` (number): cumulative distance all agents have moved
- `timeScaleHistory` (array of numbers): stack of previous timeScale values for undo
- `agentPositions` (array of {x, y, z}): current positions of all remaining agents
- `nanDetected` (boolean): true if any NaN was ever detected and corrected
- `conservationCheck` (boolean): true if agentCount + evacuatedTotal === 80 at all times
- `resetCount` (number): how many times the simulation has been reset
- `exitBToggleCount` (number): how many times Exit B has been toggled
physics_constraints: Agent conservation law: agentCount + evacuatedTotal must always equal 80. No agent position coordinate may be NaN. Agents must remain within building bounds except when passing through an exit gap. Collision avoidance repulsion must prevent agent overlap below 1.2 units. timeScale must be clamped to [0.0, 5.0]. Simulation time must advance proportionally to timeScale * dt when not paused.
